title: Sebastian and the Tide
premise: When a water-damaged letter postmarked eleven years ago washes up in the tide pools below Quentin Halloran's lighthouse, it turns out to be the goodbye she never sent — and the reason her first love, the ferryman's son Rowan Ashe, vanished without a word. Rowan returns to the island to settle his late father's estate, and the two are forced to relive the night the letter was lost: a storm, a missed train, and a choice between family duty and each other. As Quentin drafts a novel that keeps becoming their real story, they must decide whether love is something inherited like the lighthouse itself, or something chosen anew. In the end, Quentin lets Rowan stay past the last train — and lets herself be written into a life with no safe steps at all.
about_author: Lior Whitlock is the pen name of a former maritime archivist who spent six years cataloguing letters recovered from coastal shipwrecks. They now write from a converted signal station on the northern coast, where the tide still delivers other people's unfinished business.

chapters.title: What the Tide Brings Back
chapters.summary: Quentin, tending the decommissioned lighthouse she inherited from her grandfather, finds a sodden letter in the tide pools addressed in her own handwriting. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: unease — the past has physically returned, and she recognizes the date before she dares read it.

chapters.title: Eleven Years of Small Safe Steps
chapters.summary: Flashback woven through present routine: Quentin's carefully ordered life as a part-time novelist and keeper of small rituals. She burns nothing, reads nothing, locks the letter in the lamp room. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: controlled dread; safety revealed as a kind of hiding.

chapters.title: The Ferryman's Son Returns
chapters.summary: Rowan Ashe steps off the morning ferry to settle his father's estate, and the whole island watches them nearly collide at the dock. Neither mentions the letter. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: electric, wary recognition — twelve years collapse into one glance.

chapters.title: The Estate of Silences
chapters.summary: Rowan sorts his father's belongings and finds evidence his father intercepted mail that final autumn — including something from Quentin. He says nothing, but begins asking old neighbors careful questions. POV: Rowan. Emotional beat: guilt curdling into resolve.

chapters.title: Chapters That Keep Becoming Us
chapters.summary: Quentin's novel-in-progress stubbornly writes itself into the story of the night they lost each other. Her editor loves it; she hates what it costs her. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: creative compulsion as confession by another door.

chapters.title: Storm Warning
chapters.summary: A gale forces Rowan to shelter at the lighthouse when the last ferry cancels. Trapped together overnight, they circle the old wound without naming it. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: warmth laced with danger; proximity makes denial impossible.

chapters.title: The Lamp Room
chapters.summary: Quentin discovers Rowan found the locked letter's twin among his father's papers. A furious, tender confrontation: who was allowed to grieve, who was lied to, and by whom. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: rupture — the safe steps finally crack.

chapters.title: The Night of the Missed Train
chapters.summary: Full flashback: the storm eleven years ago, the elopement plan, the father who hid the letter, the train that left without them. Both POVs interleave for the first time. Emotional beat: devastating clarity — they were both abandoned by someone else's duty.

chapters.title: Inheritance
chapters.summary: Rowan learns the ferry lease — and his father's debts — pass to him if he stays; Quentin faces the historical trust that wants the lighthouse decommissioned and sold. Duty arrives wearing both their names. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: suffocating weight of legacy.

chapters.title: Let Someone Stay After the Last Train
chapters.summary: Quentin offers Rowan the keeper's cottage for the winter. The island gossips; her editor warns the novel is becoming too true to publish safely. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: reckless hope — the first unsafe step taken on purpose.

chapters.title: Learning Each Other Again
chapters.summary: A quiet middle movement: shared meals, repaired shutters, Rowan reading her drafts aloud, Quentin teaching him the light's old rhythms. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: tentative joy, love reassembling from salvaged parts.

chapters.title: The Trust's Letter
chapters.summary: Official notice: the lighthouse must be vacated by spring unless Quentin proves continuous family keeping. Rowan's ferry lease demands he return to the mainland by December. Two clocks start ticking. POV: Rowan. Emotional beat: dread — history threatening to repeat as paperwork.

chapters.title: What I Never Sent
chapters.summary: Quentin finally reads the recovered letter aloud to Rowan in the lamp room. It is not a goodbye; it was a plea to wait. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: catharsis and grief entwined — mourning the years, not the person.

chapters.title: The Editor's Deadline
chapters.summary: Her publisher wants the novel finished by New Year's; writing the ending means choosing an ending for herself. Rowan quietly books a mainland interview. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: pressure mounting from every direction at once.

chapters.title: Father's Ledger
chapters.summary: Rowan uncovers proof his father kept more than one letter — years of intercepted correspondence — and that his father died holding Quentin's last unanswered page. POV: Rowan. Emotional beat: fury and forgiveness wrestling over a dead man's desk.

chapters.title: First Frost, First Fight
chapters.summary: Rowan admits he may take the mainland job; Quentin accuses him of leaving again before anyone can leave him. Both retreat wounded. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: the lowest point — old patterns reasserting under new pressure.

chapters.title: The Empty Manuscript
chapters.summary: Quentin deletes her novel's final chapter; she cannot end it because she refuses to choose. The lighthouse goes dark during a maintenance failure, and she sits alone in the black. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: surrender — the moment before change.

chapters.title: Relighting
chapters.summary: Rowan comes back through the storm to help relight the lamp, and in the beam's return they finally say everything: the letter, the father, the fear, the want. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: reconciliation — honest, unsentimental, chosen.

chapters.title: The Hearing
chapters.summary: Before the island council, Quentin argues the lighthouse's living history; Rowan publicly surrenders the ferry lease to testify on her behalf, burning his own inheritance to do it. POV: Rowan. Emotional beat: sacrifice made visible — duty inverted into devotion.

chapters.title: Last Train Out
chapters.summary: The winter solstice, the anniversary of the original missed train. The mainland job offer expires at midnight; the last ferry leaves at nine. Rowan stands at the dock with a ticket. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: climax — history offering the same door twice.

chapters.title: Stay
chapters.summary: Quentin runs the cliff path in the wind and asks him — out loud, plainly, no letters this time — to stay after the last train leaves. He lets the ferry go without him. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: triumph of choice over fate; the word 'stay' as vow.

chapters.title: Sebastian and the Tide
chapters.summary: Spring: the trust grants the lighthouse reprieve, Quentin finishes the novel with a new ending, and they name the gull Sebastian who steals breakfast from the lamp room sill every morning. POV: alternating, closing on both. Emotional beat: resolution — love as a thing tended daily, like a light.
